name: Pleroma Codex
tag: A guided way to study Gnostic texts and ideas, with readings, a glossary and notes on how scholars read them.

scenarios.title: Start a guided study path
scenarios.ask: I am {level} with Gnostic texts. Build me a {weeks} study path with {mins} a day.
steps: Path builder
Planned {=weeks * 5} sessions, five a week, starting with short passages and moving to longer texts.
Reading guide
Opens with selected sayings from the Gospel of Thomas, which survives in a Coptic copy found among the Nag Hammadi codices in Egypt in 1945.
Glossary agent
Introduces about {=weeks * (2 + level)} key terms, such as Pleroma, Aeon, Sophia and Demiurge, each in plain words.
Context agent
Adds a note where scholars disagree, so you see more than one reading of a passage.
Review agent
Sets a short recall question at the end of each week.
followups: It is a Greek word meaning 'fullness'. In many Gnostic texts it names the divine realm. The codex shows how different texts use it rather than giving one fixed definition.
No. The codex is educational. It presents the texts, their context and scholarly views, and leaves belief to you.
Yes. At {=mins * 2} minutes a day the same path takes about {=ceil(weeks / 2)} weeks.

scenarios.title: Compare one idea across texts
scenarios.ask: Show me how the idea of {concept} appears across {texts} texts in the codex.
steps: Search agent
Found {=texts * concept} passages that mention or describe {concept} across {texts} texts.
Comparer
Lined up the passages side by side and marked shared themes and clear differences.
Context agent
Added short notes on each text's likely setting and how scholars group it.
Glossary agent
Linked related terms so you can follow the idea into other parts of the codex.
followups: Do all Gnostic texts tell the same story?
No. 'Gnostic' covers a range of groups and writings, and they differ a lot. That is why the codex shows passages side by side instead of one summary.
The codex marks the translation used for each passage and lets you load another one you have access to.

scenarios.title: Prepare a study group
scenarios.ask: I lead a study group of {people} people meeting for {sessions} sessions. Prepare guides for each meeting.
steps: Path builder
Chose one reading per meeting, kept short enough to read aloud in about 10 minutes.
Question writer
Wrote {=sessions * 4} discussion questions, mixing close reading with open reflection.
Context agent
Added a one-page background sheet for each reading.
Planner
Suggested pairs for small-group talk: {=floor(people / 2)} pairs per meeting.
followups: Can members use the codex at home?
Yes. Each member can follow the same path on their own and add private notes.
How do you keep discussion balanced?
The guides include questions that ask what the text says before asking what people think, which keeps the group anchored in the reading.
